Commentary.Commentary: The away side would be a bit disappointed though as Holder and Gabriel added 35 for the final wicket but will be more or less satisfied. When they come out to bat, first they would aim to negotiate the remaining 10 minutes before Lunch safely. Whereas, Windies will be aiming to pick quick wickets. Join us shortly.

Earlier, the home side got a strong foundation after a fall of an early wicket, courtesy three 50-plus stands and a century stand. Kraigg Brathwaite once again stood tall and stroked a fine ton. For the tourists, Mehidy Hasan was the wrecker-in-chief as he took a fifer and was a constant threat on a slightly two-paced track.

It has been a brilliant comeback from Bangladesh to bowl out the hosts for just over 350. The young pacer, Abu Jayed was in his elements in the morning and sent both the overnight batsmen, Shimron Hetmyer and Roston Chase packing quite early. The southpaw who had batted so well would be disappointed to miss out on a ton. His wicket led to a series of dismissals, as the hosts lost their last 6 wickets for only 59 runs.

OUT! Chopped on! Abu Jayed finishes with a 3-fer. Length delivery around off, Gabriel pushes at it but only manages to an inside edge which goes onto deflect onto the stumps. WINDIES ARE BOWLED OUT FOR 354!
FOUR! This will sting Bangladesh! Slower in pace and slightly overpitched as well, Gabriel lifts it over mid on to find the fence.
Back of the hand slower ball from Jayed again. Gabriel plays it uppishly but it falls well short of the mid off fielder.
On a length well outside off, Shannon goes at it with hard hands but finds the cover fielder.
Outside off, pushed through covers and Holder yet again takes the single on the second ball of the over.

FOUR! Hit with aplomb! Shortish ball on middle and off, sits up nicely for Holder. He stands tall and hammer-pulls it over wide long on. Has bisected the two fielders in the deep to perfection for a rocketing boundary.
Safely negotiated! Full length ball on off, Gabriel leans ahead and dead-bats it.
Angling in sharply from a length to go past Gabriel's defense to hit him on the pads.

FOUR! Bangladesh can't afford to relax. Every run can hurt on a track which is somewhat two-paced. Pitched up ball around off, Gabriel swings at it but the ball goes off the outer half of the bat over the gully region. No protection in the deep and the No. 11 picks up his second boundary.
Back of a length ball, answered with a straight bat.
The batsman has driven it through mid off. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Short ball on middle, pulled away nicely to deep mid-wicket for a brace.
Outside off, Gabriel pushes at it but misses.

Not Out! Going down leg! Bangladesh lose both their reviews. Back of the hand slower ball from Jayed. It foxes Gabriel to hit him low on the pads. The bowler is really confident and seeing that, the skipper signals the 'T'. The replays roll in. The third umpire checks for the front foot no ball. It is just fine. The Snicko doesn't spot any nick and Hawk Eye shows that the impact is umpire's call while the ball is missing the leg stump.
Abu Jayed feels that he has trapped Shannon Gabriel in front of the stumps and Shakib Al Hasan takes the review. Seems to be really close to the naked eye.
On a driveable length outside off, Gabriel goes for a drive but gets it off the inner half down the track.

A chirpy appeal for an LBW turned down! Good length ball on off, seaming in after landing. Gabriel tries to block it but seems to have got an inside edge onto his thigh pads. The visitors are interested but the umpire shakes his head.
Holder takes the run, having enough trust in Gabriel to survive the remaining four balls in this over. Full outside off, pushed to covers to rotate strike.
Full delivery wide outside off, Holder goes after it but gets beaten.
Change of ends for Abu Jayed.
Islam hits the deck hard and it is rising on Gabriel. He rides the bounce and defends it stoutly.
Length ball around off, kept out watchfully.
Similar length ball around off, eased off the back foot to extra cover.
FOUR! Good shot from the No. 11. He would be proud of that shot. Back of a length outside off, Gabriel waits for it and dabs it late past the slip cordon to find the fence.
On a length, tucked through mid-wicket for a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Kamrul Islam is back on.
Slow through the air, defended solidly.
Uppish but safe! Stops a bit on the pitch, inducing a false stroke from Jason. The ball goes past the cover fielder and a run is taken.
SIX! Hit with authority! Good going from Holder. He is trying to help his side reach 350. Once again in the slot, Holder lines it up and tonks it over long on to clear the fence with ease.

Safe! Outside off, Jason decides to leave it. Nurul waits and then takes the bails off as he feels that Holder is losing a bit of balance. The square leg umpire takes it upstairs. Well, Holder's back foot did slid for a moment but it is grounded.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
SIX! Clean as a whistle! Tossed up delivery, in the arc of Holder. He lifts it down the ground for a maximum.
Taking off after pitching and goes past Gabriel's defense to hit him on the forearm.
Survives the hat-trick ball! Leans ahead a touch and blocks it nicely.
Shannon Gabriel is the last man in.

OUT! 4th 5-wicket haul in Tests for Mehidy! He is up and running in joy. What a morning this has been for Bangladesh, they have bounced back with aplomb. Bowls this one slower through the air and lands it on middle and leg, Cummins plays around it as he tries to flick it but is hits him flush on the pads. Bangladesh appeal and the umpire obliges in a jiffy. Well, the replays show that it would have gone over the stumps. Cummins can consider himself unlucky.
Miguel Cummins is the new man in.

OUT! Keemo Paul departs without troubling the scorers on his debut! Mehidy takes a 4-fer, he has been brilliant throughout. Tossed up ball on middle and off, spinning in. Paul prods forward to defend it but seems to have gloved it onto his pads. The ball lobs towards Mominul Haque at short leg and he takes it. The visitors are already celebrating and the umpire waits to see if the players appeal. Once they appeal, up goes the finger. However, Keemo goes for the DRS straightaway. The replays roll in and there is certainly some glove on it. The on-field call is upheld.

Review time! The debutant, Keemo Paul has been ruled out caught at short leg but he straightaway decides to go for the review. Seems gone though. This is his first game, therefore he might have gone for it.
Similar ball, clipped to mid-wicket this time.
Tossed up ball on middle and leg, played with soft hands in front of square leg. A run taken.
On the stumps, the ball is defended back to the bowler.
This time he shows the full face of the bat in an attempt to defend but the ball takes the outside edge and goes on the bounce to second slip.

Ohkay! Did not see that coming! What does Keemo Paul do on his very first ball? He tries to hit it over the mid-wicket fence. What happens? He misses. The keeper whips the bails off and appeals but the batsman has not dragged his foot out.
Drinks have been taken! Meanwhile, Keemo Paul is the new man in.

OUT! The morning just keeps getting better for the visitors. Taijul Islam gets his second. He tosses it up on middle, this one pitches and then turns away. Dowrich pays the price for playing it across the line. He closes the bat face early and that induces a leading edge towards covers. Mehidy Hasan there takes it on the second attempt and then tumbles onto the ground. Dowrich walks back cheaply and Bangladesh are now into the tail.
Floats it up on middle, Dowrich drives it to covers.
Flatter on off, Dowrich goes back and punches it to mid on.
Stump-to-stump line, pushed back towards the bowler.
Spinning down the leg side, tucked to fine leg to rotate strike.
Slow through the air outside off, patted to the cover region.
Fullish on off, knocked down to long on for a single.

Sharp turn! Tossed up on middle and off, spinning in. Holder comes forward to deal with it but seems to have missed it and gets hit on the pads. A casual appeal from the visitors but they cut it short quickly, realizing it is going down leg.
Floated outside off, pushed off the front foot to covers.
Mehidy Hasan comes onto bowl for the first time this morning.
Nice! Now follows it up with the arm ball. Holder tries to defend but the ball goes off the inner half towards square leg for a run.
BEATEN! Nicely bowled again! On off, this one also pitches and turns away. Holder does not play for the turn and is beaten by it.

Spin and sharp spin there! Flighted ball outside off, Holder tries to drive it through the off side but misses. The keeper collects it and whips the bails off quickly. The players appeal but the umpire is unmoved.
Flighted ball on off, Holder drives it to covers.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Flatter on off, the batsman off the back foot keeps it out.
Good length around off, Dowrich guides it to point.
Another ball way down the leg side, swings away further. No chance for the keeper this time who dives to his left, he does get a glove to it but can't stop the bye.
Down the leg side, maybe the bowler here is tiring  a touch. The keeper does well to dive to left and collect it.
Back of a length on off, kept out.
Fuller in length on off, Holder drives it to mid off.

EDGY BOUNDARY! Windies won't mind how it comes and from where it comes as long as it comes. This is on the shorter side outside off, Holder off the back foot tries to punch it through the off side but the ball takes the outside edge and goes to the third man fence.

Edged but runs! Nicely bowled by Taijul. He floats it up outside off, the batsman goes for the booming drive through the off side. It induces the outside edge and goes through short third man. The man from point hares after it and does well to push it back in with a dive. Saves a run for his side.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Extra bounce there! Quicker on off, this one shoots after pitching. Holder does well to defend it onto the ground.
Flighted ball on off, Holder defends it off the front foot.
Floats it up on off, the batsman keeps it out.
The slider on leg, Holder tries to flick but misses to get hit on the pads.
Taijul Islam is into the attack.
Another length ball outside off, the batsman makes a leave.
On a length around off, it is pushed to covers.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Fuller in length outside off, the batsman shoulders arms to it.
Fuller in length on off, defended.
A little too short outside off, the batsman slaps it to covers.
Quicker on off, it is guided towards point.
Flighted ball on off, kept out.
Works it through mid-wicket and gets to the other end.
FOUR! Excellent use of the wrists! This is on the pads, Dowrich plants his front foot forward and whips it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Floats it up on off, defended.
Driven towards the mid on region.
Good length around off, Holder guides it to point. A wicket maiden for Abu Jayed.
On the stumps this time, Holder off the back foot pushes it to mid off confidently.
Fuller in length outside off, Holder makes his third leave in a row.
Another ball outside off, Holder does not fiddle with it.
Outside off, left alone.
Jason Holder walks out to the middle.

OUT! Three reds and another one bites the dust! Both the overnight batsmen have now been dismissed. On top of that, Windies also lose a review. It is once again Abu Jayed who has struck. One would wonder why didn't he bowl more yesterday. Nevertheless, the Bangladesh players are all pumped up at the moment. This is bowled on a length around off, comes back in after pitching. Chase tries to flick but misses to get hit on the pads. The players appeal and the umpire raises his finger. Chase walks upto his partner and after a chat goes for the review. Replays show no inside edge and Hawk Eye shows three reds.
The question is asked for an LBW and the umpire raises his finger. Chase is the man in question as he signals for the 'T'. Looks close.
Driven through mid off by the batsman. They pick up a single.

Almost another one! This is bowled close to the leg pole. Dowrich goes down on one knee and tries to sweep. The ball stays a touch low which beats the bat of Shane. It goes agonizingly close past the leg pole and also between the keeper's legs for a bye.
Flighted ball on off, Chase drives it down towards mid off for a run. 300 up for the Windies.
A low full toss on leg stump, Chase hits it down to mid on.
Fires it on the pads, Chase tries to flick but misses to get hit on the pads.
Slower through the air on off, Chase drives it hard to covers.
Another ball outside off, the batsman need not play at those.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Back of a length on off, Dowrich pushes it to mid off. Playing his shots is the wicket-keeper batsman. Just shows how confident he is.
Way too wide outside off, the batsman need not play at those.
Back of a length again on off, Chase guides it through point for a run.
On a length and outside off, Chase makes a leave.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
This one has pitched in the similar area but goes on with the arm. Dowrich prods forward and plays for the original trajectory.
Turn for Shakib! He slows this one up outside off, Dowrich lunges and tries to keep it out but is beaten by the away turn.
Works it with the angle through square leg for a run.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Flatter and on off, Chase pushes it to covers.
Shortish and outside off, Dowrich cuts it to the man at point.
Shane Dowrich is the new man in.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! No hundred for Hetmyer as Abu Jayed provides the ideal start for the visitors. Excellent delivery this. He lands it on a length around off, he bends his back on this one as it takes off after pitching. Also straightens a touch. Hetmyer tries to defend it off the back foot but the ball kisses the outside edge and goes into the mitts of the keeper. The players appeal and the umpire raises his finger. Hetmyer walks back dejected but he has played a very good hand for his team. Half the side now back in the hut for the hosts.

Beauty! The change of angle almost does the trick. The bowler goes around the wicket and angles it into the batsman. Hetmyer has to play at it and he does so with a forward defense. The ball pitches and then moves away beating the outside edge.
Once again the delivery stays a touch low! On a length around off, Hetmyer pushes it to mid off.
Wide outside off, Hetmyer slashes at it but mistimes it to covers.
Shorter in length outside off, Hetmyer tries to drag his pull through the leg side but mistimes it to mid-wicket.
Flighted ball on off, the batsman keeps it out off the front foot.
Slower through the air on middle, Chase works it to the man at mid-wicket.
The arm ball on off, Chase goes back and keeps it out.
Floats it up on off, not a lot of purchase from the wicket for Shakib. Chase prods forward and defends it.
Fires this one on off, Chase lunges and keeps it out.
Works it with the turn through mid-wicket and gets to the other end. The run also brings up the 50-run stand between the two, 4th of the innings.
Shakib Al Hasan to bowl from the other end.
Just one from the first over! This is bowled on a back of a length around off, Chase guides it to point.

This one stays a little low! There were some cracks on the wicket and that must have pitched on one of them. However, the batsman need not worry as it was not on the stumps. Outside off, Chase makes a leave.
Closer to the off pole this time and on a shorter length. Chase hops and defends it onto the ground.
Slightly fuller than the last two deliveries but the line is outside off. Chase lets it be.
Back of a length again on off, Chase off the back foot pushes it to covers.
And Hetmyer is underway! He is now 15 short of his maiden Test ton. This is bowled on a back of a length around off, Shimron works it through mid-wicket and gets to the other end.

We are all set for the action to begin. Out come the Bangladesh players and they are followed by Roston Chase and Shimron Hetmyer who will resume their innings. The latter will be on strike and he will be facing Abu Jayed who will start the proceedings for the visitors. Here we go...

Bangladesh on the other hand, will hope for a few quick wickets. It will once again be their spinners who will do the majority of the bowling today. The wicket did provide assistance to them yesterday and Shakib will hope it does today as well, so that his bowlers can make full use of it. Will we see a fightback from the visitors or will the hosts continue their domination? Stay tuned for the all-important first session in a while. Welcome to the coverage.

Day 2 of the second Test between Windies and Bangladesh. The hosts dominated the proceedings on Day 1 and today they will look to tighten their grip on the game. They are 5 runs short of 300 and have six wickets in hand. The platform is set for them to post a big first innings score and that is exactly what they will be hoping for.
... Day 2, Session 1 ...

Three consecutive fifty-plus stands after the fall of an early wicket has meant that the home side continue to sail on. There have been moments of exhilaration for Bangladesh but not enough to put any pressure on the opposition. The visitors for a change need to be on fire on the morning of Day 2 and trigger a collapse or else it will be the Windies who will keep on hogging the limelight. Join us on Friday at 1000 Local (1500 GMT) to catch all the action. Till then, cheers!

Shakib Al Hasan showed much more faith in his spinners in this game. That owes to a couple of factors - there were a few cracks on this surface as well as some extra bounce on offer and the other point is that spin is their major strength. It was Mehidy Hasan who utilized the conditions to the optimum to pick up three wickets. He could have had a couple more had his fielders given him proper support. The rest of the bowlers were not consistent enough. Taijul Islam did send the centurion back but he was a little wayward overall.

Final session - 27 overs, 131 runs, 1 wicket. The most productive phase of play for the Windies in terms of runs. Sums up the day nicely for the hosts and they are right on top at the moment. Kraigg Brathwaite continued to be solid as a rock after Tea and scored a well-deserved ton. Shimron Hetmyer played the perfect foil to him. The youngster showed intent, played some eye-catching strokes and has given his side a really nice foundation, also nearing his maiden ton in Tests.
Mahmudullah drags his length back. Hetmyer camps back and punches it to sweeper cover for a single. THAT'S STUMPS ON DAY 1!
Gives this one a lot of air as Shimron leans ahead and taps it to mid off.
On middle and leg, Hetmyer turns it through fine leg and comes back for a brace.
Nicely bowled! Slow through the air, Hetmyer leans ahead to defend but the ball whizzes past the outside edge of his bat.
Outside off, pushed to covers.

That is close! Coming in with the arm as Hetmyer is on the move as he tries to play it defensively but the ball goes off something towards the keeper. The ball slips out of his hand and hence, he can't effect a stumping. The ball rolls beside the stumps as Nurul Hasan appeals but the umpire is unmoved. Seems like it might be going down the leg side and hence, they don't take the review. The replays show that the ball struck the front boot of the batsman but it was missing the leg stump.
Mahmudullah returns at the fag end of the day. He has one over to create some impact.
Slow through the air, Chase plays it with an angled blade past gully and comes back for a brace.
This one stays a bit low. Roston does well to crouch and dead-bat it.
On a flatter trajectory, Chase camps back and cuts it to extra cover.
A touch quicker on off, eased off the front foot to mid off.
Outside off, it is slow through the air and hence, Hetmyer has a lot of time to place it through point. A run taken.
Played with the spin to mid-wicket.
Taijul Islam is back on.
On the pads this time, defended solidly off the front foot.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot. They pick up a single.

Not where he intended but a fair enough result. A wider ball outside off, Hetmyer goes after it and slashes it but gets it off the outer half of the bat. The ball goes towards sweeper cover and a couple of runs result.
Very full delivery, knocked down through mid on for a run.
Outside off, eased to sweeper cover for a single.

SIX! Clean as a whistle! He is looking like he belongs at the highest level. He spots Mehidy giving the ball a lot of air and steps out of the crease at the right moment. A nice extension of the arms, a lovely followthrough of the bat as he lifts this one with beautiful timing. Away she goes down the ground. She is going, going and clears the fence with ease. First maximum of the game.
FOUR! Crisp! Shakib bowls this one full outside off, inviting Chase for an expansive stroke. Roston obliges this time and creams it through covers to find the ropes.
Slow through the air again, Roston shapes up to drive it through the line but checks his shot at the last moment and defends it back to the bowler.
Floated ball, Chase leans ahead to block it.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Outside off, pushed off the front foot to covers.
Slow through the air, spinning in, defended solidly.
Sits back to the quicker one and keeps it out.
Almost a replica of the previous ball as Roston clips it to the same region.
Played with the spin to mid-wicket.

What happened there? Is that a hit wicket? Probably not. Hetmyer punches this one through extra cover for a run but the a bail is out of place at his end. The fielder in the same region has his hands up but the keeper quickly points out that it's him.
Spinning into Chase who tucks it through mid-wicket to rotate strike.
Shorter in length, cut away with the spin to sweeper cover for a single.
Slower through the air, Roston puts his head down and defends it calmly.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Shakib drags his length back. Shimron camps back and defends it with authority.
FOUR! Shot! A touch short outside off, Hetmyer rocks back and cuts it against the spin through covers to find the fence.
On middle and leg, tucked to the leg side for a single.
Well bowled! Coming in with the arm, Chase is tentative in coming forward and gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Shakib Al Hasan comes back for his final spell of the day. Can he pick up a wicket?
Tossed up ball, Chase milks it through mid on for a single.

FOUR! That could have been dangerous! Spinning down leg, Chase goes back and works it through fine leg. Abu Jayed runs across to his right, and tries to keep the ball in play with his foot but when he is in contact with the ball, his foot is already touching the ropes. He then loses his balance and crashes into the advertising boards. No harm done though. We saw Kusal Perera injuring himself in a similar way recently. Needs to be careful.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

In line of the stumps, tucked through mid-wicket. The non-striker is waiting, waiting, waiting as he sees the fielder coming in but finally responds to the call of his partner. Single safely taken in the end.
Leg Bye! Spinning into Chase as he goes for the big sweep but the ball brushes his pads and rolls past the keeper. A run taken.

That was tantalizing for the batsman! Smart bowling from Mehidy. He gives this one a lot of air outside off and gets it to turn in appreciably. Chase leans ahead to defend but gets an inside edge onto his pads. The ball lobs up in the air but falls down on the pitch itself.
In the channel outside off, Shimron lets it go.
He needs to be careful not to get carried away! Full delivery wide outside off, Hetmyer goes after it but misses.

FOUR! Pulled and pulled with authority! This young man certainly packs a punch. Just a fraction short and that is all the youngster needs to line it up. Gets into the position quickly and hammer-pulls it through wide mid on for a rocketing boundary.
Comes around the wicket and bowls it on off, Hetmyer pushes it back to the bowler.
Good length on off, Hetmyer pushes it to covers.
Fuller in length on off, Chase drives it towards mid off for a run.
Outside off, Shimron leans ahead and eases it to covers. A productive over for Mehidy Hasan and Bangladesh.
Slow through the air, turned through mid-wicket for a run.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.

Four Byes! Turn and bounce! Almost got the better of Chase on the first ball itself. Tossed up around off, takes off after pitching to go past the attempted push of the batsman. The ball goes over the stumps and the keeper is beaten as well as the ball rolls to the fence behind.
Roston Chase is the new man in.

OUT! GONE! One shot too many from Brathwaite and he loses his wicket. Nevertheless, a brilliant innings by the opener comes to an end. He walks off to a standing ovation from the crowd. The 109-run stand also comes to an end. Coming back to the ball, Brathwaite uses his feet, just like he did on the last delivery. Tries to go over mid-wicket just like he did on the last ball. This time though, he does not get the elevation and the ball goes towards Taijul Islam at short mid-wicket who takes it. Hasan gets his third and Bangladesh would hope they can take a few more before Stumps.
FOUR! Once again effective use of the feet! He hits it with the spin over the mid-wicket region and into the fence.
Time for spin again as Mehidy Hasan to roll his arm over. He was productive with the new ball in the morning and will be aiming to be on the money once again.
Swinging into Hetmyer as he remains well balanced and clips it to the man at mid-wicket.
Back of a length ball, answered with a straight bat.

Loose from the youngster! Needs to learn that in order to succeed in Test cricket, you have to be sensible with your shot selections and also have a plethora of patience. On a driveable length, leaving the southpaw. He chases it with hard hands but the ball whizzes past the outside edge.
Jayed switches to over the wicket and again gets some shape on that! It is shaping in as Shimron covers the line and eases it to mid off.

Well bowled! Almost got the better of Hetmyer there. Jayed steams in from around the wicket and bowls a full length ball around off. The ball swings in substantially. Shimron is a bit late to react but manages to jam it out towards mid on.
Back of a length ball well outside off, Kraigg waits for it and times his punch to perfection towards sweeper cover. Will get a single for doing so.
Very full ball outside off, Shimron jams it out through backward point and comes back for a brace. 7 from the over.
There is some issue with the ball and the umpire has a look at it. Seems to be fine at the moment.
A half-volley on the pads, clipped away nonchalantly to deep mid-wicket to rotate strike.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Streaky! On a driveable length outside off, Hetmyer goes for a full-blooded drive but gets a thick inside edge past the leg stump. A run taken.
On the hips this time, Hetmyer hops and tucks it around the corner for a brace. That brings up the 100-run stand between the duo. They have mixed caution with aggression to perfection.
Short of a length and some width on offer, Kraigg punches it off his back foot through point and comes back for a brace.
Kamrul Islam to share the second new ball from the other end.

FOUR! 2nd Test fifty for Shimron Hetmyer! The youngster has been positive from the word go and has played an entertaining innings. Full length ball well outside off, Hetmyer slices it behind backward point and the ball races to the fence. Has a big smile on his face and is applauded by his teammates in the pavilion.
Kamrul Islam is warming up.
Similar length ball in the same zone, placed nicely through cover-point for a run.
Back of a length just outside off, Kraigg shuffles across and works it to mid on.
Already signs that this track is slightly two-paced! Length ball in the off stump corridor, keeps a touch low. Brathwaite adjusts in his crease to stonewall it.
On a length outside off, played with an angled bat towards the fielder at point.
Pitched up ball around off, Brathwaite leans ahead and eases it towards mid off.
The second new ball is now available and it has been taken straightaway. Abu Jayed to steam in first up with the red cherry.
Drinks!
Fuller in length, Kraigg leans ahead a touch and places it through mid on for a run.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Coming in with the arm, turned to the leg side for a run.
Slow through the air, defended solidly.
Similar delivery, same result as Hetmyer defends it.
Turning away from Hetmyer who goes back and blocks it.
Loopy delivery this time, Kraigg leans ahead in defense.
Goes deep in the crease and defends this one with authority.
Floated delivery, defended solidly off the front foot.
On a flatter trajectory, kept out watchfully.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Four Leg Byes! Shoddy stuff from Bangladesh. Down the leg side, brushes Brathwaite's pads and rolls past the keeper to the fine leg fence.
Driven towards the mid on region. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Flatter on off, Hetmyer pushes it through covers and takes a run.

Century for Brathwaite! Consecutive ones for him. He becomes the first Windies batsman to do so since 2009. His 8th in this format. A innings full of temperament, application and determination. He has rode his luck but take nothing away from the way he has played. He taps this delivery towards point and gets to the other end. Takes his helmet off and acknowledges the applause from the crowd and his teammates. He would now want to make it a daddy hundred.
Uses his feet but mistimes it to mid-wicket.
Flatter on the stumos, Kraigg defends it.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Mahmudullah is back on.
FOUR! Dances down the track and goes with the spin. Connects well and finds the mid-wicket fence.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

A huge appeal by the keeper! The arm ball on off, Brathwaite guides it towards point and moves onto 99. The keeper appeals as he feels it is pad first but the umpire is not interested. Now then, Bangladesh have missed a chance here. Hawk Eye shows that was pad first and also three reds which means the on-field call would have been overturned. Once again luck favoring the Windies and Brathwaite.

TWO Byes! A beauty there by Islam! He angles this on middle and then gets it to turn square. Brathwaite tries to flick but misses. The ball beats the keeper and hits the hand of the diving slip fielder and goes down towards fine leg. The batsmen run two.
Slower through the air on off, defended.
Works it towards mid-wicket. He wants a run but is sent back.
Taijul Islam is back on.
Fuller on the pads, Kraigg flicks it through mid-wicket and takes a run. He moves onto 98 and keeps strike for the next over.
Back of a length on middle, Hetmyer pushes it towards mid on for a single.
FOUR! Slashed and slashed hard! Another wide delviery outside off, Hetmyer pounces on the width offered and hits it through backward point for a boundary. He moves onto 41.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Full and wide outside off, Hetmyer slashes it through point and runs two.
Back of a length on off, Hetmyer keeps it out.
FOUR! Moves onto 97! Similar to the last delivery, the only difference is, this time he finds the gap. Uses his feet and whips it through mid-wicket.
Uses his feet and whips it to the man at mid-wicket. He makes a good stop there.
Swept and swept fine but finds the fielder at deep square leg for a run.
Floats it up on off, kept out.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Down the pads, Brathwaite goes back and works it towards backward square leg. The fielder there does well to dive to his right and make a good stop. A single taken.
Shorter in length outside off, Hetmyer mistimes it to covers.
On a length around off, Brathwaite cuts it through point and gets to the other end. He moves onto 92. Also 200 up for the hosts.
On a length around off, Brathwaite keeps it out.
Back of a length on off, Kraigg hops and defends it onto the ground.
Almost! Lapse of concentration? Maybe! Slightly short and outside off, Brathwaite goes after it away from his body but luckily for him the ball does not take the edge.
A good start by the pacer! Comes running in and lands it around off, this one shapes away. Brathwaite pokes at it and gets beaten.
Kamrul Islam is back on.
Worked around the corner for a run.
Flighted ball on middle, Kraigg keeps it out.
Down the leg side, Brathwaite defends it onto the ground.
Ball hits the batsman low on the pads.
Flicks it to mid-wicket.
Works it to short fine leg with the turn.
From over the wicket Shakib bowls it full on middle, Brathwaite works it down to long on for a run.
Uses his feet and eases it down to long on for a single.
Slightly shorter outside off, Brathwaite punches it through covers for a quick run.
Loopy ball on off, defended.
Flights it up on off, this one turns back in. Hetmyer tries to defend but gets it off the inner half past short leg for a run.
Works it against the turn through the leg side for a run.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Gives it air on off, defended.
Flatter on middle, Hetmyer pushes it back towards the bowler.
Uses his feet and drives it to covers.
Floats it up on off, the batsman keeps it out.
The arm ball on off, Hetmyer steps down and tries to defend but the ball goes off the inner half to mid-wicket.
Stays within the comfort of his crease and keeps this one out.
Slower through the air, Kraigg lunges in defense.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.
Tossed up delivery, eased down to long on for a run.
On middle and leg, defended towards short leg.

Brilliant running between the wickets! Sliding down the leg side with the arm, Brathwaite tickles it past the keeper as the fielder chases it. Hetmyer calls his partner for the third run and is lightning quick between the wickets to complete it. Good game awareness. Kraigg is on 87 now, a number which is considered the devil's number. Can it work in favour of Bangladesh?
Shakib Al Hasan returns for a bowl.

Another appeal! Strange by Hetmyer. He walks down the track but does not get to the pitch of it. He then thinks about leaving it as he tries to make his way back in the crease. The ball brushes his pads and goes into the mitts of the keeper who whips the bails off and starts appealing for something. Not sure for what, maybe the LBW. The umpire though is unmoved as the impact was way outside. End of an action-packed over.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Fires it on off, SH pushes it to covers.

DROPPED! Tough chance this one! Mehidy could have easily had two in his last 4 deliveries. But as they say, when it is not going your way, it just won't. Hasan tosses it up on off, this one also turns away sharply. Hetmyer goes for the booming drive but the ball takes the outside edge and goes towards first slip. Liton Das there dives to his left, gets fingertips to it but can't hang on. The batsmen take two. Also, the third consecutive 50-run stand is up for the Windies in this innings.
Works it with the turn towards mid-wicket for a run.
On the pads, Brathwaite fails to flick and the batsman gets hit on the pads.
The batsman has driven that ball straight back.
FOUR! Creamed! Hetmyer gets down the track and gets to the pitch of it. He smashes it through covers.
Down the leg side, Hetmyer works it fine down the leg side for a brace.
Cuts it through the off side and takes a run.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Uses his feet and drives it to mid off.

A stumping chance goes abegging! Brathwaite gets a life. Bangladesh needed to take that chance. Mehidy is very unlucky there. This was beautifully bowled. Flighted delivery outside off, inviting the batsman to drive. Kraigg does so but the ball turns back in sharply. The ball goes between bat and pad and just over the stumps. Brathwaite also drags his back leg out of the crease but to his luck, the keeper fails to collect it. To add salt to the wound, the ball races to the fine leg fence for FOUR BYES. How costly is this going to be?
On the pads, worked to short fine leg.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Flatter on off, Brathwaite keeps it out.
Action replay of the last delivery.
Works it with the turn to the man at square leg.
Mehidy Hasan to bowl from the other end.
Uses his feet and drives it back to the bowler. A good start to the session for the Windies.
FOUR! Second boundary in the over! A poor delivery again, down the leg side. Hetmyer flicks it fine down the leg side and another boundary results. He quickly moves onto 22.
Another ball on the stumps, this time Hetmyer defends it onto the ground.
Shorter in length outside off, Kraigg pushes it through covers and gets to the other end.
Good batting by the southpaw. He works this through mid-wicket and gets to the other end. Follows the boundary with a run.
FOUR! Ideal start to this session for the Windies. A gift, a half-tracker outside off, Hetmyer cuts it through point and bags himself a boundary.

We are back for the final session. Due to the good over rate we have only 25 overs left in the day's play. So we aren't in for a long one. Brathwaite and Hetmyer resume their innings. The latter will take strike and he will be facing Taijul Islam who will start the proceedings. Here we go...
... Day 1, Session 3 ...

However, Brathwaite is going strong, is nearing a ton and is getting good company from the young Hetmyer. Though the track has eased out a bit, there is still some sharp turn and extra bounce on certain occasions. The visitors need to utilize that properly and keep chipping away at the wickets. Otherwise, the hosts might run away with the show. Join us for the final session in a while.

Session Highlights - 30 overs, 85 runs, 1 wicket. The Windies have gone about their business pretty nicely and are placed in a comfortable position. However, Hope will be ruing the fact he didn't convert his start into a big one. Once you settle at the crease in the longest format of the game, you shouldn't throw your wicket away. Credit to Bangladesh for believing in themselves and it was Taijul who broke the 79-run stand.
A half-volley outside off, Shimron leans ahead and caresses it through covers. Rahim gives it a long hard chase and manages to save a run for his side. Three runs taken. THAT SHALL BE TEA ON DAY 1!
Spinning in sharply, Brathwaite leans ahead and controls the flick towards the man at 45. A run taken.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Hangs back in the crease and works it to short leg.
Tossed up outside off, Hetmyer uses his feet and strokes it to extra cover for a run.
FOUR! A gift and that has been duly accepted! Half-tracker outside off, right in the arc of Hetmyer. He lines it up, rocks back and slaps it through covers to find the fence.
On a flatter trajectory, Hetmyer knocks it down to long on for a run and will keep strike.
Loopy delivery, pushed off the front foot towards mid off.

Four Byes! These are bonus runs for the Windies. Spinning down the leg side, Hetmyer is unsure whether to flick it or pull it. Tries to pull it away eventually but misses and so does the keeper. A boundary results.

Down the leg side, Shimron fails to put bat on ball. Once again, Nurul collects it and flicks the ball onto the stumps but no harm done. The ball deflects towards covers but the keeper runs after it to deny the overthrow.
Islam drags his length back and Brathwaite cuts it away towards point to rotate strike.
Floated outside off, Kraigg prods forward in defense.
Straighter one this time, pushed back towards the bowler.
Uses his feet to this one but is not quite to the pitch of it and hence decides to block it.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Slower through the air, kept out from within the crease.
On a flatter trajectory, answered with a straight bat.
Nervy! Fullish ball around the pads, Hetmyer is early into his flick as a leading edge is induced but the ball rolls towards covers safely.
Mehidy Hasan is back on.
Similar ball, similar reaction from the batsman.
Outside off, left alone.

Some good work from Nurul Hasan but Brathwaite did well to maintain his balance. Down the leg side, Kraigg tries to flick it but misses. Hasan moves to his left and flicks the ball onto the stumps but the batsman's back foot is firmly inside the crease.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
On a shorter length, Brathwaite rocks back and cuts it towards backward point.
Spinning away, Kraigg goes back and defends it.
The length was not that short but somehow Hetmyer managed to pull it away. He hangs back and drags it towards mid-wicket for a couple.
Streaky! Floated around off, Brathwaite plays for the turn and gets a faint outside edge past the keeper. A run taken.
Full ball on the stumps, Kraigg opts to hang back and block it. Should have been forward to that.
Spinning down the leg side, Kraigg pads it away.
Slow through the air outside off, pushed gently to the cover region.

Coming in with the natural around the wicket angle. Hetmyer plays for the non-existent turn and hence, gets an outside edge. The ball goes through the gap between slip and silly point. A single taken.
Outside off, spinning away. Kraigg lets it be.
Slow through the air, kept out watchfully.
Played to the point region by the batsman.
Islam switches to around the wicket and bowls a full ball on middle, Hetmyer works it through mid-wicket to change strike and gets off the mark.
On a flatter trajectory, Shimron rocks back and cuts it but finds extra cover.
Tossed up generously around off, Hetmyer lunges in defense.
Slower through the air on the pads, Kraigg flicks to to mid-wicket.
FOUR! A poor ball and Brathwaite takes full toll of it! Short and on the pads, Brathwaite pulls it through backward square leg and the ball races to the fence.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.
Works it to the man at mid-wicket with the turn.
Floats it up on off, the batsman lunges and keeps it out.
Down the leg side, the batsman works it fine for a couple.
On a flatter trajectory, Hetmyer uses the depth of the crease to block it solidly. A wicket maiden for Taijul Islam.
Fuller in length, patted towards mid on.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Hangs back to this one and keeps it out.
Shimron Hetmyer comes out to bat.

OUT! Big, big wicket for the visitors! They needed this badly and Taijul has come to their rescue. Islam tosses this one nicely around off and the ball is spinning away. Hope takes a long stride forward in order to block the ball but he is not quite to the pitch of it. The ball takes off after pitching, hits his gloves and lobs towards the vacant silly point region. Nurul Hasan behind the wickets is sharp as a hawk. He runs swiftly towards it and dives full length to catch it. The Bangladeshis appeal vociferously but Shai himself starts to walk. Good sportsmanship from him. The 79-run stand has been cut short. Can the tourists capitalize on this?
Loopy delivery, defended solidly off the front foot.
Spinning into Brathwaite as he hangs back and plays it defensively to the leg side.
Similar delivery as Kraigg is astute in his defense.
Shorter in length, kept out watchfully.
The batsman works it down the leg side.
On middle and leg, clipped with the spin to the leg side.
Slow through the air outside off, Kraigg pushes at it with hard hands but gets an inside edge onto his pads.

Where did that come from? Vicious turn and bounce. Pitches on middle and off and takes off with some appreciable away spin. Brathwaite is squared up as the ball brushes his gloves and goes past first slip. A run taken.
This one is well outside off as Kraigg doesn't fiddle with it.
Tossed up ball, Kraigg leans ahead to push it to covers.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot. One run added to the total.
Comes ahead to the loopy ball and dead-bats it.
Played with the spin past point to rotate strike.

Safe! The impact is outside off, clearly! A review goes down the drain for Bangladesh. Floated outside off, spinning in. Hope shuffles across in order to block it but is pinged on the pads. Mahmudullah appeals vociferously but the umpire stays put. The bowler has a chat with his skipper and Shakib decides to signal the 'T' after taking his time. Time for the replays. The Snicko doesn't detect any nick. The Hawk Eye rolls in and the impact is miles outside off, end of the story.

Finally some action happening for the visitors. The man in question is Brathwaite and the referral is against an LBW decision. Shakib thinks a lot about it and after a chat with Mahmudullah, takes the review. Seems that the impact is outside off.
Outside off, tapped towards third man for a run.
The batsman allow the ball to come to him and works it away towards mid-wicket.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Stump-to-stump line from Mahmudullah as Kraigg leans ahead in defense.
Spinning into Brathwaite as he turns it around the corner.
A bit uppish but no harm done! Turning away from Hope as he slices it to the point region.
On a flatter trajectory, Shai Hope hangs back and defends it nicely.
Loopy delivery outside off, pushed off the front foot to covers.
Shorter in length, ample time for Kraigg to sit back and cut it towards point. A brisk run taken.
Islam gives this one more air and bowls it a touch outside off. Brathwaite opens the face of his bat to play it to gully.
Slow through the air around off, defended solidly off the front foot.
Hangs back to the quicker one and punches it out.
Spinning in, Kraigg makes use of the depth of the crease to work it through mid-wicket. A run taken.
Fuller in length, played with soft hands to mid off.
Turning in from outside off to go past the defense of Brathwaite and hit him on the pads. No appeal for LBW as the impact was way outside off.
Shorter in length, kept out from the comfort of the crease.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Mahumudullah is into the attack for the first time.
That's a peach! Lands on off and turns away sharply to go past the hanging bat of Hope.
Well outside off, Shai leaves it alone.

Howzat? Probably not. Slow through the air on off, turning away. Hope leans ahead to defend but is beaten all ends up. Nurul Hasan is quick as lightning to take the bails off but Shai's back foot is firmly behind the crease it seems. The close-in fielders appeal but the square leg umpire doesn't refer it. Yes, the replays show that Hope is safe.
A bit wider outside off, Hope lets it go.

Good timing! Pitched up delivery outside off, Hope leans into it and strokes it through extra cover. Two fielders, one from long off and another from sweeper cover are after it but the former reaches it eventually. A couple taken.
Some turn and bounce for Taijul but Brathwaite deals with it quite nicely. Plays it with soft hands past the first slip fielder to get to the other end.
Islam hits the deck hard for the third time in this over but not much venom on it as Shai ducks under it.
Back of a length and some room on offer, Kraigg plays it with an angled blade through backward point. The fielder from gully chases it and keeps it down to only a single.
Another bumper, Kraigg sits under it in a jiffy.
Short of a length ball on middle and leg, turned towards mid-wicket.
A well-directed bouncer around off, equally well played by Brathwaite. He arches his back, drops his wrists and sways away from the line of the ball.
Back of a length outside off, Hope rises on his toes to punch it through cover-point. A run taken.
Only 11 overs have been bowled between the pacers till now but even in those 11 they haven't looked threatening.

Drinks! So the first hour after Lunch belongs to the Windies. The duo of Brathwaite and Hope has continued the good work and the two have now stitched a partnership in excess of 50. Windies will hope for the two to carry on. Whereas, the visitors will need to pick a few quick wickets.
Fires it on the pads, the batsman misses the pull shot. The ball hits the pads and goes down to fine leg for a leg bye.
Flatter outside off, the batsman guides it through point for a brace.
Driven through the covers by the batsman.
FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries! Due to the last ball the bowler this time drags his length back. Bowls a half-tracker outside off, Brathwaite cuts it through point and gets a boundary.
FOUR! Lovely use of the feet by Kraigg. He gets to the pitch of the ball and hits it past mid on for a boundary. He moves onto 60.
Slower through the air outside off, the batsman lets it be.
On off, defended.
Fuller in length on off, Hope tries to drive but gets it off the inner half towards the bowler.
Length ball around off, the batsman defends it to mid on.
On the pads, easy for Brathwaite as he flicks it through backward square leg for a run.
On middle, Hope works it through mid on for a run.
Fuller in length on off, this one swings away. Hope mistimes it to covers.
Floats it up on off, the batsman prods forward and defends it.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Quicker outside off, the batsman cuts it to the man at point.
Flatter on off, the ball pitches and then turns away but it is slow turn. Hence the batsman has time to adjust and defend it.
Floats it up on off, the batsman drives it down to long off for another single.
Tosses it up on off, Brathwaite eases it down to long off for a run.
Taijul Islam is back on.
Pulled well but finds the man at square leg! Short and on off, Hope pulls it to the fielder at that position.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Hits the length again on off, Hope prods forward and defends it onto the ground.
On a length on middle, defended.
Works it with the angle around the corner for a run.
Fuller on off, Kraigg drives it through covers.
A bouncer to end the over! Hope ducks under it.
Full on the pads, a batsman of Hope's quality will not miss out. He flicks it through mid-wicket and bags a brace.

Overthrows! The ball is hit towards mid on and the batsmen set off for a run. The fielder there has a shy at the non-striker's end but misses. There is nobody backing up and the batsmen run two more. That brings up the 50-run stand between the two. Consecutive ones for the Windies in this innings. They though would hope these two can make it big.

Full again and he gets some shape into the batsman. The line however is down the leg side. The batsman misses the flick to get hit on the pads. There is a stifled appeal from the players but nothing doing.
Pitched up gentle ball outside off, Kraigg pats it towards mid off.
A bit of extra bounce there! Takes off from a length as Brathwaite is surprised. He manages to fend it off eventually.
The batsman has edged that one.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

Fifty for Brathwaite! His 18th in this format. He continues his form against Bangladesh. Doesn't he love playing against them? His job though is yet not done. He would now want to convert it into a triple-digit score. He guides this length ball down to third man for a single to get to that milestone.
Works it with the angle to the man at mid-wicket.
On the stumps, Hope defends it onto the ground.
On a length around off, kept out off the back foot.
Kamrul Islam is into the attack.
Fuller and outside off, the batsman makes a leave.
Third in a row but this one is down the leg side and Hope has no qualms in ducking under it.
Second bouncer and once again the batsman ducks under it.
A bumper down the leg side, the batsman ducks under it.
Back of a length on off, the batsman hops and keeps it out.
On a length and outside off, Hope shoulders his arms to it.
Very slow and outside off, the batsman lets it be.
Flatter and outside off, it is cut to point.
Down the leg side, Kraigg works it fine and runs two.
Very full on off, the batsman drives it back to the bowler.
Slower through the air on off, the batsman defends it.
Floats it up on off, the batsman lunges forward and defends it.
A bouncer down the leg side, Hope lets it be.
Wide outside off, once again the batsman watches it go through to the keeper.
Fuller in length on off, it is driven to covers.
Wide outside off, left alone.
On a length around off, kept out.
Length on off, KB pushes it to mid on for a quick run.
Eases this through mid on and gets to the other end. 44 is the stand between the two.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Once again! His favorite shot! Brathwaite punches it through covers and bags a brace.
FOUR! Bread and butter stuff for Kraigg! This is short and outside off, KB goes back and cuts it through point for a boundary. 100 up for them.
OOOO! Slower through the air on off, it pitches and then turns away. Brathwaite first thinks about playing at it but then looking at the turn lets it be. Good leave in the end.
Strokes it to covers with the turn.
Shakib Al Hasan is into the attack for the first time in this session.
On a length outside off, left alone.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
An in dipper on middle, Brathwaite misses the flick. The ball brushes the pads and goes towards fine leg and the batsmen run a leg bye.

A halt in play! Some extra work for the fielders as they have to carry the advertising board and put it back behind the boundary. It was blown onto the field by the wind which is very strong at the moment.
Fuller in length on middle, KB drives it to mid on.
Bowled on a length and outside off, Kraigg tries to defend but gets an outside edge towards backward point.
A bumper outside off, left alone.
A dot to end a productive over for the Windies. 11 from it. Hope works it with the turn to the man at mid-wicket.
FOUR! Second boundary in the over! Once again Hasan pays the price of bowling it too full and offering width. Hope prods forward and strokes it through extra cover.
Flatter on off, Hope defends it off the back foot.

FOUR! Excellent shot! Not easy to hit an off spinner who is turning the ball through the off side. It is another loopy delivery outside off, Hope reaches out for it and strokes it through covers for a boundary.
Floats it up outside off, Hope reaches out for it and strokes it through covers for a brace.
Eases it with the turn towards mid on for a run.
A beauty to end! On off and it swings away. Hope is drawn into the stroke as he tries to defend. He plays inside the line and the ball whizzes past the outside edge. A maiden by Jayed.
Has to be consistent with this line! On off and Hope defends it with a straight bat.
Third leave of the over as once again it is bowled outside off.
Length again but he needs to bowl it closer to the off pole. For now it is outside off, the batsman need not play at it.
Better as he lands it on a length around middle, it is worked to mid-wicket.
A little too wide outside the off stump to make the batsman play.
Flatter on off, pushed to covers. End of Hasan's first over in this session. Did not get a lot of purchase in this over.
Down the leg side, left alone.
Fullish on off, driven to mid off.
On the stumps, defended.
Flights it up on off, Kraigg lunges and keeps it out.
Fires it on the stumps, KB keeps it out.
Mehidy Hasan to bowl from the other end.
Good length on off, kept out. A good start for the Windies after the break.
Very wide outside the off stump. The bowler wanted the batsman to go after it away from his body. Hope is happy to let it be.
Goes full again but on the stumps this time. KB works it to mid on and sets off for a run. The fielder has a shy but misses.

FOUR! Streaky but effective! Full and outside off, Brathwaite tries to jam it out but the ball takes the outside edge and goes to the third man fence. First runs in this session and it is in the form of a boundary.
Fuller in length again on off, the batsman defends it solidly.
Starts off with a full ball on middle, this one comes back in a touch. Kraigg works it to square leg.

We are back for the afternoon session. 35 overs were bowled in the first one and we can expect a good over rate to be maintained in this one as well. Kraigg Brathwaite and Shai Hope will continue their innings. The former will be on strike and he will be facing Abu Jayed who will start the proceedings for Bangladesh. Will he be given more than an over? We will have to wait to watch as he comes running in to bowl the first ball of this session.
... Day 1, Session 2 ...

The Windies would hope the two can now build a big partnership after Lunch. They though will have to tackle a lot of spin on a wicket which is providing assistance to the spinners. Bangladesh on the other hand, will look to make full use of the conditions and take some quick wickets. Join us for the second session in a while.

A mixed session is what we witnessed! After electing to bowl, the visitors struck early by removing Smith. Powell and Brathwaite then steadied the ship with a fifty-run stand. The former once again perished after getting a start. He fell prey to Mehidy who was the most impressive of the Bangladesh bowlers. The away side would have surely liked another before the break but Hope, who then joined Brathwaite ensured they head into the break unscathed.
Another delivery on the stumps which has been played out nicely by Hope. THAT WILL BE LUNCH ON DAY 1!
Better from Hope! He lunges out and blocks this down onto the ground.
Nicely bowled! Loopy delivery on off, it dips on the batsman. Hope drives it uppishly but well short of covers.
Almost! The arm ball by Shakib on middle. It takes the inside edge of Brathwaite's bat as he tries to defend, beats the short leg fielder and goes towards square leg for a run.
On the pads, it is clipped through mid-wicket for a run.
Floats it up on off, it is guided to point.
Shakib Al Hasan to bowl the last over of this session.
Once again it is on the stumps and the batsman blocks it.
Gives it air on off, kraigg defends it on the off side.
Works it with the angle to mid-wicket.
Flighted ball on middle, kept out.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Played to mid-wicket region by the batsman.
Flatter on off, kept out.
Played to mid-wicket region by the batsman.
On middle, hit to mid on.

Howzzaat? The answer to that question is not out! The off spinner outside off, Brathwaite lunges and tries to defend but is beaten by the turn into him. The ball hits his pads and the players appeal but the umpire shakes his head. Height looks to be an issue and Hawk Eye shows my judgment to be right. Going over.
Very full on off, it is hit back to the bowler.
Quicker on middle, it is tucked to mid-wicket.
Fuller on off, Hope strokes it through cover-point and runs two.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Uses his feet and drives it through mid off for a run.
On off, it pitches and turns. Brathwaite tries to defend but gets an outside edge towards point.
Slightly outside off, left alone.
Flighted ball on off, Hope drives it down to long off for a run.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground. A maiden by Hasan.
On the pads, KB tries to flick but misses once again and the ball hits his pads.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Another big appeal but the umpire is not interested! Flatter on middle, this one turns back in. The batsman lunges forward to defend but misses to get hit high on the pads.
Down the leg side, the batsman lets it be.
Flatter on off, the batsman off the back foot defends it.
Flatter on off, Hope punches it to covers. Another tight over comes to an end. Runs not easy to come by at the moment.
On the shorter side outside off, Brathwaite cuts it through point for a run.
Driven through the covers by the batsman.
Flighted ball on off, kept out.
Misfield and a run taken! It is driven back to the bowler who lets it through his legs and the batsmen take a run.
Flighted ball on off, it is driven through long off and the batsman gets to the other end.
Comes around the wicket and bowls it full outside off, the batsman drives it through extra cover and runs a single.
Down the leg side, the batsman pads it away.
Very full on the stumps, it is hit back to the bowler.
Plays it with the turn to mid-wicket.
Very full on middle, the ball is mistimed to the bowler.
On the pads, worked to short leg.
Eases it through mid off for a run.
Loopy ball on off, the batsman defends it onto the ground.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
On the stumps, defended.
Another flighted ball on off, it is driven back to the bowler.
Floats it up on off, kept out.
Taijul Ismal is back on.
The batsman works it down the leg side.
Quicker on middle, Hope defends it off the back foot.
Floats it up on off, kept out.

Leading edge! Mehidy is having a good time with the ball! He slows this up on middle, Hope tries to work it through the leg side but closes the face of the bat a touch early. He gets a soft leading edge to covers.

Almost drags it on! Another flatter delivery and outside off, this one comes back in. Brathwaite tries to cut it against the turn but the ball is a little too close to play that shot. It takes the inside edge and goes agonizingly past the off pole and down towards fine leg for a run.
Fires it on the pads, Kraigg works it to leg slip.
Nicely played! He plants his front foot foward and drives it to covers.
Another couple, this time through the off side. He once again lunges and strokes it through covers for a brace.
Loopy ball on middle, Hope keeps it out.
Floated on off, it is driven to covers.
Good batting! Hope uses his reach and makes this tossed up delivery into a full toss. He flicks it through wide mid on for a couple.
Clips it with the angle through square leg for only a single.
Flatter and outside off, KB guides it through point for a run. End of another successful over for Hasan.
Pushes it against the spin and through covers for a run. Hope gets off the mark.
Works it with the turn to the man at square leg.
Shai Hope is the new man in.

OUT! Mehidy strikes again! He provides the breakthrough and breaks the stand which was looking really good out there. Once again Powell falls after getting a start. This was plumb and Mehidy knew it. He bowls the straighter one on off, it comes in with the angle. Powell plays for the away turn but there ain't any. He misses and the ball hits him low on the front pad. Hasan is already on a celebratory run as he is appealing. The umpire also agrees with him and raises the finger. Powell walks up to his partner and has a discussion but then opts against the review. Rightly so, as Hawk Eye later on shows three reds.
Uses his feet once again but Hasan sees it. He fires it on the pads. Powell tries to flick but misses to get hit on the pads.

Plays it with the turn down to long on and jogs to the other end. That run also brings the 50-run stand up. Good recovery from the two, especially after they lost an early wicket. They need to go on now.
On the stumps, kept out. Doing well here is Powell. He has got off to a start but can he continue?
FOUR! Fourth boundary of the innings for Powell and this one is probably the best of the lot! This is tossed up outside off, Kieran goes down on one knee and slaps it through covers.
Quicker on off, Powell defends it off the back foot.
Slower through the air on middle, Powell tries to whip it but misses to get hit on the pads.
The short of length delivery has been cut away through square on the off side.
Eases it through long off for a run.
Gets behind the line of the delivery and defends it.
FOUR! This should release all the pressure that was building! It is short and outside off, Powell says thank you and cuts it through point for a boundary.
Down the leg side, Powell tries to flick but misses.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
An appeal but to no avail. Floats this on off, again it turns away. Powell lunges and tries to defend but he is beaten. The slip fielder takes it and appeals but the umpire does not agree.
Good bowling! Fires this on the leg stump, it turns away. Powell tries to work it across the line but gets a leading edge to point.
Once again juts an over for the pacer as Mehidy Hasan is back on.
Down the leg side, Brathwaite pads it away.
Flighted on the stumps, KB defends it.
Fullish on off, Powell drives it to mid off for a quick run.

NOT OUT! Umpire's call! Not a bad review by Bangladesh. That could have gone either way. Powell could consider himself a touch lucky. He dances down the track but does not get to the pitch of the ball. It turns in sharply and Powell is taken by surprise. He does not offer a stroke as the ball hits his back pad. A huge appeal follows but the umpire shakes his head. Shakib after a thought signals the 'T'. Time for the replays which show the ball to be clipping the leg pole. Bangladesh though do not lose a review.

Review time! A huge shout for LBW against Powell has been turned down. Shakib after giving it a long thought has gone for it. It could be a good one by Bangladesh. The question is, has Powell offered a shot?
Very full on middle, Brathwaite works it through mid-wicket for a run. He moves onto 22.
Slower through the air on middle, no purchase for the bowler this time. KB easily defends it onto the ground.
Shakib Al Hasan is back on.
Fullish outside off, the batsman makes a leave.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
A bumper on middle, Powell tucks it towards mid-wicket. Brathwaite wanted a run but is rightly sent back by his partner.
Goes fuller in search of some swing but there ain't any. KP drives it to extra cover.
Back of a length on off, Powell defends it off the back foot.

Edged and a good stop! A loosener by Islam first up. Slightly short and outside off, Powell looks to punch but it takes the outside edge and goes to the left of the second slip fielder. He dives and makes a good stop with one hand. Saves a boundary.
Kamrul Islam is into the attack.
Outside off, the batsman need not play at those. Just two runs from the over.
Turn but the line is on leg stump, Powell works it through square leg and gets to the other end.
A little too full on off, the spin is now out of contention. KB eases it down to long off for a run.
On the shorter side, Brathwaite fails to capitalize on it as he cuts it straight to cover-point.
Slower through the air on off, Kraigg keeps it out.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.

Time for Drinks! After only the sole over from the pacer, Abu Jayed at the start of the innings, Shakib Al Hasan decided to introduce himself. Since then, the spinners took center stage and kept on asking some questions on a track where there is some extra bounce. After losing Devon Smith, the Windies have done well to keep the opposition at bay. Kraigg Brathwaite needs a mention as he has used his feet nicely and is showing others the way how to bat on this surface. It seems that the visitors will back their strength which is spin. An interesting passage awaits us.
Pushed through the air outside off, Kraigg leans ahead and eases it through covers for a run.
Landing around off and spinning in, defended to short leg.
Spinning down leg, all Brathwaite has to do is get some bat on it and he does that. The ball goes towards fine leg and a couple is taken.
Kraigg covers the line to the tossed up ball and defends it right under his eyes.
Uses the depth of the crease to this one and punches it away to rotate strike.
FOUR! Poor delivery and duly punished! A half-tracker around off, Powell rocks back and pulls it with authority through mid-wicket for a rocketing boundary.
Shorter in length, blocked watchfully.
Slow through the air, defended nicely.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. They pick up a single.

Powell needs to be patient! That is what Test cricket demands. Tossed up on off and turning down leg sharply, Powell exposes his stumps and goes for the big sweep but misses. The extra bounce on the track means that the ball goes over the stumps. Otherwise, he would have been dead there.
Pitching around the pads and skidding through as Powell decides to pad it away.
Floated ball, Kraigg eases it through mid on to change strike.
Stump-to-stump line, Powell reads the length quickly and turns it through mid-wicket. A couple taken.
Outside off, left alone.
Floated up nicely, defended solidly off the front foot.
Hangs back to the shorter ball and defends it nicely.
Down the leg side, Powell tries to flick but misses.
Beaten comprehensively! This is good bowling from Hasan. He lands it at a quicker pace on middle and off and gets it to turn away sharply. Powell hangs his bat in anticipation but gets foxed.
Mehidy Hasan is back on.
Spinning away from around off as Kraigg doesn't fiddle with it.
The length is short which allows Powell to rock back and cut it past point for a run.
Played away with the spin to the leg side.
The batsman works it down the leg side.
Mominul Haque has taken a blow on his helmet and his teammates check on him. The physio comes out as well. Such blows are always risky but thankfully, he seems to be fine.

Is that dropped? Well, Mehidy Hasan could have converted that into a catch. Tossed up ball, Powell nails the slog sweep as Monimul at short leg turns behind to take evasive action. The ball hits the back of his helmet and deflects over first slip. Mehidy Hasan stationed there, dives backwards but the ball just goes past his fingertips and falls on the ground. Haque seems to have been shaken up.
On middle and leg, worked with the spin to mid-wicket.
Islam is varying it up nicely as he bowls this one full, Kraigg lunges in defense.
Quicker and shorter, left alone.
Tossed up ball, spinning away, Brathwaite comes down the track and drags it towards mid on. Got a bit foxed there and the shot selection was not correct.
Landing around off, played with the spin to mid off.

FOUR! Brathwaite is trying to apply pressure on the spinners and it is working for him at the moment. Can prove to be a good ploy. He uses his feet to the tossed up ball and lifts it over mid on to pick up another boundary.
Floated up nicely on middle, Powell comes ahead to deal with it but gets it off the inner half of the bat past the left side of short leg. A run results.
Spin again but this time it is a different one. The left-arm spinner, Taijul Islam will have a bowl now.
Nice revolutions on this one, Brathwaite watches it closely and taps it to mid off.
Similar delivery, the result is the same.
Spinning away as the right-hander cuts it to point.
Tight off stump line, Kraigg comes forward confidently to dead bat it.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Coming in with the arm, Brathwaite hangs back in defense.
On a flatter trajectory, Powell is astute in his defense. 6 from the over.

Close shave! There are some balls which are taking off on this track and are causing problems for the batsmen. This one has extra bounce as well. Kraigg tries to defend but the ball deflects off his gloves past the left side of the leg slip fielder. A run results.
Slower in pace, kept out watchfully.
FOUR! Brathwaite is growing in confidence! Good intent from him. Skids down the track to the tossed up ball and heaves it over mid-wicket for a one-bounce boundary.
Spinning in as Kraigg turns it off the inner half towards leg slip.
On a shorter length, kept out from the comfort of the crease.
Another ball on the stumps and Kraigg negotiates it well. A maiden by Shakib and a good one.
Flighted ball on off, KB prods forward and defends it onto the ground.
Works it with the angle to the man at mid-wicket.
Uses his feet and tries to get to the pitch of the ball. Does not do so but does well to defend it onto the ground.

Lovely delivery and equally well played. Good cricket all around. Flatter and on off, this one straightens and shoots off the surface. Kraigg does really well to keep it down off the back foot. He played that with soft hands.
Floats it up on middle, a touch too full. Brathwaite lunges and defends it.
Fuller ball outside off, sliced away to point.
FOUR! Shot! First boundary for Powell. On a flatter trajectory and the length is on the shorter side. Powell rocks back and cuts it past backward point to find the fence.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Kraigg is nimble on his feet as he works it through mid-wicket to rotate strike.

An appeal for an LBW but turned down! Mehidy tosses this once nicely on middle and gets it to spin in. Brathwaite leans ahead to defend but is hit on the pads. The visitors go up in unison but the umpire shakes his head. The bowler looks at Shakib but he doesn't take the review. Rightly so, as the replay shows it would have spun down leg.

Nicely done! When the spinners are bowling in tandem, you need to use your feet. Powell does just that and clips the fullish ball through mid-wicket. The fielder from the same region hares after it, slides near the fence and keeps the ball in play. Three runs taken. Shakib lauds the effort.
Pitches on off and spins away to open Brathwaite up in his stance. He manages to block it off the back foot.
Coming in with the angle, clipped through mid-wicket for a couple.
On a flatter trajectory, defended from the comfort of the crease.
Slow through the air, Kraigg comes down the track and keeps it out.
Leans ahead again and blocks it right under his eyes.
Slow through the air, defended nicely off the front foot.
Outside off, left alone. A successful over for Hasan.
Shorter in length, cut away with the spin to backward point.
Uses his feet to this one and blocks it.
The batsman charges down the wicket. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Streaky! On middle and off and squares Powell up. He tries to block it but gets an outside edge past slip. A run taken.
Kieran Powell comes out to bat.

OUT! Mehidy Hasan draws first blood! The ploy to bowl with spin with the new ball has reaped dividends for Bangladesh. Smith was not looking that assured against the spinners and he has finally fallen. Hasan tosses up the ball on a fullish length on middle and leg. Devon is a bit off-balanced as he falls over a little in an attempt to clip it and seems to have got an inside edge onto his pads. The ball lobs up in the air towards square leg. Mominul Haque and Nurul Hasan are after it but the former reaches it first from short leg and pouches it safely. The players appeal and up goes the umpire's finger. Ideal start for the visitors.
Similar delivery, kept out from within the crease.
Nice pace and line from  Shakib as Kraigg lunges in defense.
Loopy delivery, defended solidly off the front foot.

Edged but safe! Tossed up nicely on middle as there is some bite from the surface. Smith comes ahead in an attempt to keep it out but only manages to get an inside edge. Liton Das at leg slip dives to his right but the ball goes agonizingly past him. A run taken.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Uses his feet to this one but is not quite to the pitch of it and hence, blocks it.
Slow through the air around the pads, Brathwaite opts to pad it away. Pretty safe as it probably pitched outside leg.
Hasan has gone a bit off radar against Brathwaite. Spinning down leg again and Nurul is quick to react.
Brathwaite is assured with his footwork as he clips it against the spin to mid-wicket.
Full on middle, eased to mid on.
Similar delivery, on this occasion Kraigg leaves it.
Going down with the arm, Brathwaite missed but Nurul doesn't as he collects the ball nicely.
Leg stumpish line, spinning down. Devon tries to clip it away but misses. A good take from Nurul Hasan. Two consecutive maidens.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.
Shorter in length, kept out watchfully.
Shakib spots Smith using his feet and hence, bowls it in the blockhole. The southpaw jams it out to mid on.
Well played! Full ball on middle, Kraigg clips it through mid-wicket and the timing is good on that. The fielder chases it and saves a run for his side.
Floated ball, eased to mid off.
Turning and bouncing away sharply as it is left alone.
Slow through the air, played gently to covers.
On a flatter trajectory, blocked neatly off the back foot.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Spinning away as Smith plants his front foot across to allow it through.
Loopy ball outside off, Devon goes at it but gets an outside edge but the ball falls short of second slip who dives and stops it.
Shorter in length, defended from within the crease.
Nervy moment! Lands on off and spins away appreciably. The key is that Brathwaite goes at it with hard hands. Even though an edge results, it falls short of first slip.
Tossed up generously, kept out watchfully.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
This time Kraigg drives it with the spin to covers.
Brathwaite comes ahead and leaves this away spinning delivery.
Loopy delivery, played with soft hands to covers.
This one is wider outside off, the reaction from Devon is the same.
Outside off, left alone.
Ooh... uppish! Pitches on off and turns away with extra bounce. Smith goes at it with hard hands and mistimes it. The ball goes on one bounce to the backward point fielder.
The batsman has pushed it to the cover region.

Four Byes! There is a lot of turn and bounce on this track and it is not a bad call from Shakib to bowl two spinners against Smith immediately. Floated around off, Smith pushes but misses and the keeper fails to collect it as well. The fielder chases it but only comes second best.
Spin from both ends. Mehidy Hasan to roll his arm over now.
Slow through the air, defended solidly off the front foot. A good start from Shakib.
Spinning away from Brathwaite who leaves it alone.

Close shave! Shakib has found his rhythm. Bowls a loopy ball on off as Kraigg tries to work it against the spin but a leading edge is induced. The fielder at mid off is interested but it falls well short of him.
Outside off, pushed to covers off the front foot.
Windies and Smith are away! Tossed up ball, clipped past short leg for a single.

Almost, almost! Starts off with a fullish ball on middle and leg, Smith is on the move as he flicks it towards short leg. By the time the fielder reacts, the ball hits his knee and deflects behind him.
Shakib Al Hasan to share the new ball from the other end.
Pitched up ball around off, patted to mid off. Jayed starts off with a maiden.
This one swings in from middle and leg as Brathwaite shuffles a touch and flicks it to mid-wicket.
On a length on off, moving away after landing. Kraigg lets it go.
Almost a replica of the previous delivery as the right-hander is circumspect in approach to make a third leave in a row.
There is not much movement on this one as the line and length is the same. Kraigg doesn't fiddle with it.
Starts off with a full length ball outside off, generates a bit of away swing as well. Brathwaite plants his front across and sees it through.
We are set to get underway. Kraigg Brathwaite and Devon Smith to open the batting for the Windies. Abu Jayed to steam in with the new red cherry. Three slips and a gully in place. Here we go...

Windies skipper, Jason Holder says that they would have probably bowled first as well. Feels that the track is hard underneath. Adds that his batsmen need to survive the initial stages. Informs there are two changes - Keemo Paul, the debutant comes in place of Kemar Roach while Devendra Bishoo makes way for Shimron Hetmyer.

Bangladesh skipper, Shakib Al Hasan says that they are going to bowl first. Adds that there is moisture on it and expects his pace bowlers to make use of it. Informs there is one change as Taijul Islam comes in for Rubel Hossain. States that they are working very hard and is hopeful of putting in a much better performance.
Toss - Bangladesh win the toss and opt to field.

PITCH REPORT - Jeff Dujon assessing the surface says there is a good distribution of grass on it. Mentions that the nature of the grass is fresh and the track is very hard too. States that there are a few cracks on it but there will be a lot of pace and bounce on offer. Reckons that the spinners will come into play as the game progresses. Ends by saying that it will be a very important toss.

The Windies have decided to rest the belligerent Kemar Roach but they still have a pace battery which can cause havoc against top batsmen. They will be striving for another clinical performance but need to be wary as the tourists will be eager to strike back. An absorbing clash is in the making.

Clear blue skies welcome us at the Sabina Park in Jamaica as we head into the second and final Test of the series. The morale in the Windies camp will be at its peak whereas it will be low in the opposition camp. When the going gets tough, the tough get going - Bangladesh not only need to believe in that fact but have to lift themselves up as well. The experienced campaigners, Shakib Al Hasan and Tamim Iqbal need to emerge as the torch-bearers in order to guide their boys.
